title: Stress Testing and Reverse Stress Testing
summary: How stress tests and reverse stress tests show the firm's vulnerabilities, how to judge whether scenarios are severe enough, and how results should shape board decisions.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How stress tests and reverse stress tests show the firm's vulnerabilities, how to judge whether scenarios are severe enough, and how results should shape board decisions.
Learning Objectives: Explain how stress and reverse stress tests are built
Challenge scenario severity, assumptions and management actions
Use stress test results in strategy, capital and risk appetite decisions
Syllabus: Scenario design: idiosyncratic, market-wide and combined stresses
Reverse stress testing: what would make the business model fail
Plausibility of management actions under stress
Integrating results into planning, capital and recovery decisions
Intended Audience: Non-executive and independent directors without a finance or accounting background
Chairs and members of board committees other than audit, and newly appointed directors
Executive directors and senior managers from non-finance functions who sign off plans or returns
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Board or senior management experience in financial services is helpful. No accounting or finance qualification is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, The Basel Framework (consolidated Basel III standards)
Basel Committee, Principles for Sound Liquidity Risk Management and Supervision (2008)
IOSCO, Principles for the Valuation of Collective Investment Schemes (2013)
